name: Kinesis
tagline: An Amazon Kinesis Data Streams endpoint the AWS SDKs talk to: shards by partition key, iterators, resharding, fan-out consumers and throttling on cue.
stands_in_for: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (Kinesis_20131202, JSON 1.1 and CBOR)
point: any access key and secret; the region comes from the signature

capabilities.title: Streams and shards
capabilities.text: Provisioned or on-demand streams; shards split the 128-bit hash key space and the MD5 of the partition key picks one.

capabilities.title: Every iterator type
capabilities.text: TRIM_HORIZON, LATEST, AT and AFTER_SEQUENCE_NUMBER, AT_TIMESTAMP; GetRecords pages with MillisBehindLatest.

capabilities.title: Resharding with lineage
capabilities.text: SplitShard, MergeShards and UpdateShardCount close parents; readers reach their end and get the ChildShards.

capabilities.title: Enhanced fan-out
capabilities.text: Register consumers and read with SubscribeToShard: an event stream that pushes records as they arrive.

capabilities.title: Retention on the clock
capabilities.text: Records expire after the retention period and iterators after 5 minutes, both on the environment clock.

capabilities.title: Java's CBOR too
capabilities.text: AWS JSON 1.1 and the CBOR the Java SDK sends by default: byte-string data, millisecond timestamps.

capabilities.title: Put as another producer
capabilities.text: Put a record from the screen or a tool; the app's consumers read it like any other.

capabilities.title: Feeds Pub/Sub
capabilities.text: A Pub/Sub import topic naming the stream's ARN reads it from TRIM_HORIZON, partition key as ordering key.

excerpts.title: A stream: its hash key space, and every record with who put it

callouts.title: Streams
callouts.text: Provisioned and on-demand streams with their open shards and record counts.

callouts.title: Endpoint
callouts.text: AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_KINESIS points the SDKs here; any key works.

callouts.title: Hash key space
callouts.text: One bar split by open shard: the MD5 of the partition key lands in one of them.

callouts.title: Closed shard
callouts.text: Records of a parent closed by a split stay readable until the retention ends.

callouts.title: Who put it
callouts.text: The app's records apart from yours and the agent's.

excerpts.title: Put a record, provoke, and the shards after a split

callouts.title: Put a record
callouts.text: Data, partition key or an explicit hash key, as another producer would.

callouts.title: Throughput exceeded
callouts.text: The next puts answer ProvisionedThroughputExceededException; the SDKs retry.

callouts.title: Reshard now
callouts.text: Splits the widest open shard; consumers must follow the children.

callouts.title: Parent shard
callouts.text: Children of a split name their parent; the parent's sequence range is closed.

provoke.name: Stream not found
provoke.what: Calls naming the stream answer ResourceNotFoundException

provoke.name: Slow puts
provoke.what: Each put waits delay_ms (3 s by default)

provoke.name: Resharding
provoke.what: The widest open shard is split now

provoke.name: Iterator ages out
provoke.what: An iterator older than 5 minutes expires for real

provoke.name: Records past retention
provoke.what: Records older than the retention are gone

advantages.title: Throttling when you want it
advantages.text: Real streams throttle only under load; here the next N calls fail, so the retry and backoff paths get tested.

advantages.title: Resharding in a test
advantages.text: Split a shard mid-test and see whether the consumer finishes the parent and follows the children.

advantages.title: No shard-hour bill
advantages.text: Streams, shards and fan-out consumers cost nothing and vanish with the environment.

advantages.title: See every record
advantages.text: Shard, sequence number, partition key, data and who put it, without writing a consumer.
